chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Magians: 'Was there a Prophet for them?' So he said: 'Yes.'

Has it not reached you the letter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to the people of Mecca: 'Become Muslims, or else I will initiate war against you'?
So they wrote to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Take the jizya (tax) from us and leave us upon the worship of the idols'.
So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to them: 'I do not take the jizya except from the People of the Book'.
So they wrote to him, intending by that to belie him: 'You allege that you do not take the jizya except from the People of the Book, then you take the jizya from the Magians of Hawar'.
So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to them: 'It was so that the Magians had a Prophet for them, but they killed him, and (they had) a Book which they burnt'.
Their Prophet came to them with their Book in twelve thousand skins of bulls.
ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Muhammad accept jizya from Magians if he said he only takes it from People of the Book?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the theological basis for the Prophet Muhammad’s acceptance of jizya from the Magians of Hawran, affirming their status as 'People of the Book' (Ahl al-Kitab) due to their belief in a Prophet and a revealed scripture. It addresses a specific historical objection where critics argued that accepting tax from idol-worshipping Magians contradicted the condition of 'People of the Book,' a point Imam al-Sadiq resolves by citing the Prophet’s own explanation that the Magians had a Prophet who was killed and whose book was burned. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for classifying Zoroastrians as Ahl al-Kitab for the purpose of taxation, distinguishing them from polytheists who do not pay jizya.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from one of our companions who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the Magians, ‘Was there a Prophet<sup>as</sup> for them?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes.
Has it not reached you a letter of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> to the people of Makkah: ‘Either you become Muslims or else we shall initiate a war against you’.
So they wrote to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, ‘If you<sup>saww</sup> could take the tax from us and leave us upon the worship of the idols’.
So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> wrote to them: ‘The taxation is not to be taken except from the People of the Book’.

So they wrote to him, intending by that to belie him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘You<sup>saww</sup> are alleging that you<sup>saww</sup> do not take the taxation from except from the People of the Book, then you<sup>saww</sup> take the tax from the Magians who emigrated’.
So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> wrote to them: ‘It was so that the Magians had a Prophet<sup>as</sup> for them, but they killed him<sup>as</sup>, and (they had) a Book which they burnt.
Their Prophet<sup>saww</sup> came to them with their Book in twelve thousand skins of bulls’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Yahya al-Wasitiy from certain persons of our people who has said the following:
“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of Zoroastrians if they had a prophet. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, they had a prophet.
Have you not heard about the letter of the Messenger of Allah to the people of Makkah? He asked them to accept Islam, otherwise, war is declared against you.
They wrote back to the Messenger of Allah asking him to receive al-Jizyah and leave them to worship their idols.
The Holy prophet wrote to them, ‘I receive al-Jizyah only from the people of the book?

They then wrote to him (the Messenger of Allah) to rebut him, ‘You think that you do not receive al-Jizyah except from the people of the book and then receive al-Jizyah from Majus (Zoroastrians) who have migrated?
The Holy prophet wrote to them, ‘Majus had a prophet but they killed him. They had a book, which they burnt.
Their prophet brought them a book on twelve thousand skins of bull?
